text:
anya: Quick sync — kicking off PRD + lightweight RFC for an "attention-mode selector" + KV retention heuristic. Reason: reduce token cost on short chats while preserving accuracy for long-context cases. Need acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and canary gating. Owners: @mike (runtime), @carla (infra), @sam (perf), @oliver (product). Can everyone add blockers by EOD Wed?

mike: ack. I'll draft the runtime API change (mode selection, fallback rules) and kernel switch hooks. question: should selector be per-request hint or automatic signal?

oliver: prefer automatic with optional per-customer override. product wants opt-in for early adopters.

carla: infra note — automatic mode implies new routing metadata and small DB for per-customer config. We should budget a migration window.

sam: Perf asks: provide p50/p95 token latency, throughput impact, and cost delta for three workloads: short-chat (<=64 tokens), mid (64-1024), long (>1024). Also include memory/KV hit-rate sensitivity.

mike: will add bench matrix. Initial heuristic idea: run 'fast-attn' kernel when prefix length < 128 and model kv-hit-rate >= 90%, else use 'compat-attn' kernel. KV retention: keep last N tokens in GPU cache for fast-attn, use sticky eviction for long-prefixs.

anya: good start. Acceptance criteria suggestions:
- No more than 5% regression in model-level generation quality on a set of representative long-context prompts (eval suite).
- P95 latency improvement >= 15% on short-chat workload when fast-attn chosen.
- No increase in OOM incidents in canary by >1 per 10k requests.
- Cost per token reduction >= 10% on short-chat traffic.

oliver: add rollout gates: unit tests + integration tests, perf benchmark baseline, small canary (1% traffic) for 48h, then regional ramp. Also require an automated rollback if error-rate or quality regressions exceed thresholds.

carla: infra asks for a feature-flagged rollout path. We'll need metrics: kernel_switch_rate, kv_eviction_rate, per-tenant mode_overrides. Can we reuse existing router labels?

mike: yes we can piggyback on router labels but need a new header "X-Attn-Mode" and server-side selector. Sample config:
```
attn_selector:
  default: auto
  thresholds:
    fast_attn_max_prefix: 128
    kv_hit_rate_min: 0.9
  overrides: /configs/tenant_attn.json
```

sam: +1. Also include a regression test harness that runs eval prompts through both kernels and diffs token-level logits. Threshold: KL divergence < 0.02 on critical prompts.

anya: Edge cases to capture in PRD: function-calling (calls must remain deterministic), streaming responses (no increased framing latency), multi-model ensembles, and multi-tenant noisy neighbor scenarios where one tenant's long-history shouldn't evict others' KV.

mike: for multi-tenant safety, propose per-alloc KV quotas and soft-eviction signals. We'll add eviction callback to surface to router for dynamic throttling.

carla: ops checklist: monitoring dashboards, SLO updates, runbook entry for rollback, and a smoke test that simulates large-concat histories.

oliver: timeline proposal: PRD by Fri, RFC draft next Tue, implementation sprint next 3 weeks, canary month after. Stakeholders: runtime, infra, perf, product, SRE.

anya: next steps: @mike create PRD doc in /docs/rfc/ and ping here with link. @sam to sketch perf matrix in the doc. @carla to list infra infra-deps. I'll consolidate acceptance criteria and rollout gates. Thanks — keep replies short, we'll sync Wed 3pm if needed. :thumbsup:
